image_description: Two individuals are seated, each holding a large woodwind instrument identified as a bassoon. The person on the right holds a reddish-brown wooden bassoon with visible metal keys and a curved metal bocal at the top. The person on the left holds a similar instrument, partially obscured. Both instruments exhibit the characteristic U-shape and upward-pointing bell of a bassoon. The setting appears to be an indoor room with furniture in the background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long wooden wind instrument of considerable height when assembled.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both instruments are visibly long, extending from the lap of the seated players to well above their heads, consistent with the ~1.3m height of a bassoon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive U-shape when viewed from front with bell pointing upward.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument on the right clearly shows the double-back tube structure forming a U-shape, with the bell section pointing upwards. The left instrument is partially occluded but follows the same silhouette.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Conical bore that doubles back on itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The internal bore structure is not visible from the exterior; only the external doubling back of the tube is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Curved metal bocal mouthpiece tube at top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A curved metal tube (bocal) is clearly visible inserted into the top of the wing joint on the right instrument. The left one is less clear due to angle/hair but likely present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Numerous metal keys and tone holes distributed along length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Multiple silver-colored metal keys and keywork mechanisms are visible along the body and boot joints of the right instrument.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bell flares outward at top and instrument held diagonally across body when played.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bell of the right instrument flares correctly. Both players hold the instruments diagonally across their torsos, supported by seat straps (visible on the right player).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dark reddish-brown polished wood finish maple or rosewood.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wood has a distinct reddish-brown hue with a polished sheen, consistent with stained maple commonly used for bassoons.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal keys are silver or gold-plated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The keywork appears silver/nickel-plated, reflecting light appropriately.
The main body segments are clearly made of wood, joined together.

artifact_observations.location: Face of the person on the right
artifact_observations.reasoning: The facial features, particularly the eyes and mouth, appear slightly distorted and 'waxy' or overly smooth, lacking natural skin pore texture. The expression looks somewhat unnatural, typical of AI generation struggles with complex facial expressions.

artifact_observations.location: Hands/Fingers of the person on the right
artifact_observations.reasoning: The fingers interacting with the keys are indistinct and seem to merge with the instrument's keywork. The anatomical structure of the hand is vague, with fingers appearing to blend into the wood/metal rather than gripping it distinctly.

artifact_observations.location: Hair and shoulder of the person on the right
artifact_observations.reasoning: The curly hair blends slightly into the dark clothing and background without a sharp boundary, suggesting minor edge bleeding or fusion.
The chair/sofa structure on the left seems to have inconsistent perspective lines, appearing slightly warped or melted into the floor area.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of woodwind instrument is indeed a bassoon and not a contrabassoon or other double-reed instrument.
To verify the physical connectivity of the metal keys to the wooden body and ensure no floating artifacts.
To audit the structural correctness of the human hands and arms holding the instrument, checking for extra limbs or impossible joint angles.
To assess overall image coherence, lighting consistency, and detect subtle generative artifacts in textures and backgrounds.
To ensure the instruments are properly grounded in 3D space relative to the players and background, checking for depth bleeding.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the hands of the musicians. AI often fails to render fingers correctly around complex objects like bassoon keys. Check if the fingers are distinct or if they melt into the instrument. Also, evaluate the facial expressions for uncanny valley effects.
